Subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Tom / Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap
- Goal: Improve internal KB search + answer generation for support docs with low hallucination and >90% grounding on our canonical KB.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + custom TF-IDF retriever, then a 7B instruction model for generation.
- Main concerns: grounding / hallucinations on policy docs, latency SLA (95th < 500ms ideally), and cost for ~1M queries/month.

Redwood recommended starting point (high-level)
1) Retrieval: dense retrieval using SBERT-style embeddings (we recommend a 768-d encoder we validated for legal/support docs) with a hybrid fallback to your BM25 for long-tail queries.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (we suggested a small cross-encoder tuned on QA pairs) to improve precision@1 for grounding-sensitive prompts.
3) Generator/model: start with a 13B instruct model we validated on similar RAG workloads; we also include a quantized 7B variant if you need lower cost for exploratory phases.

Deliverables we can provide this week
- Benchmark results from our internal PoC on a subset of your sample prompts (attached CSV).
- Proposed reranker architectures and cost/latency trade-offs (attached PDF).
- Prompt set we used + suggested evaluation metrics (shared Drive link below).

Proposed next steps
1) Share sanitized sample documents + 100 prompt examples (we've included a template: acme-prompt-sets-v1.csv).
2) Kick off a 2-week RAG eval: Redwood will run retrieval/reranker/generator permutations, return a short report with grounding metrics and recommended config.
3) Follow-up call to review results and outline a pilot (can be Dedicated or Hosted).

Can you confirm sample share timeline? If you can get the initial samples by EOD Friday (Aug 13) we can start the eval the week of Aug 16.

Attachments: acme-rag-benchmark-results.csv (sample), redwood-reranker-proposal.pdf, acme-prompt-sets-v1.csv

Thanks — happy to sync if you want a brief technical deep-dive with Vivek.

Best,

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we share samples: 

1) Embedding model: you mentioned a 768-d encoder — is this a sentence-transformers variant you run in-house or an open checkpoint (so we can reproduce)?

Hey Tom — quick technical notes to your questions: 

1) Embedding model reproducibility
- We run an in-house tuned SBERT (768-d) for support/legal style docs; it's based on the all-mpnet-base-v2 family but fine-tuned on RAG corpora for better sentence-level semantic similarity. We can share checkpoints or a Docker image for on-prem reproduction (license permitting).

2) Two-stage reranker pattern (recommended)
- Stage 1: Bi-encoder for dense retrieval (ANN, k=100). Fast and cheap.
- Stage 2: Lightweight cross-encoder reranker on top-k (we find k=10 balances throughput & precision). Use a distilled cross-encoder (e.g., cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) to reduce latency.
- If you absolutely need 95th < 500ms, we can limit cross-encoder use to only high-risk prompts (policy/legal) via classifier gating.

3) Grounding metrics we will report (examples)
- Groundedness rate: % of answers where the generator cites a retrieved doc/span.
- Precision@1, Recall@5 on annotated QA pairs.
- Hallucination rate (human-eval on a 200-example prompt set).
- Span-exact-match for factoid checks where applicable.

4) Generator variants
- 13B instruct: best quality baseline. Expected higher token cost but lower hallucination in our tests.
- 7B quantized: ~40-60% lower cost, slightly increased hallucination risk on very narrow policy language. We'll attach side-by-side outputs for the 10 sample prompts once you share.

I'll prepare a short benchmark runner and example outputs; Marissa — if you want, I can hop on the call next week to walk Priya/Tom through the runner and metrics.

Cheers,
